fixes.explanation: Idols come up in other parts of the Bible, like in Exodus 20:4, but they're not named in this verse. Verse 11 says the earth was corrupt in the sight of God, and full of violence. Verse 12 adds that all living creatures had corrupted their ways. So the word that fits is violence.

An altar is a place for offerings, and this verse doesn't mention one. God says, “Make for yourself an ark of gopher wood…” That's a build with rooms and pitch inside and out. Verse 16 adds a roof, a door in the side and three decks. So the answer is an ark.

Floodwaters. God says, “And behold, I will bring floodwaters upon the earth to destroy every creature under the heavens that has the breath of life.” Then He says, “Everything on the earth will perish.” I think this one is heavy. But notice He tells Noah ahead of time, and in the verses right before, He gives Noah the plan for the ark (Genesis 6:14).

Fire is a fair guess, since it's what a lot of us picture when we think of destruction. But verse 17 says floodwaters. Water, not flames. God says He will bring them “…to destroy every creature under the heavens that has the breath of life.” So the answer is floodwaters.

Names don't come up in this verse. God says the seven pairs are there “…to preserve their offspring on the face of all the earth.” Offspring means the young ones that come after. So the missing word is offspring, friend.

True. God said in verse 4, “For seven days from now I will send rain on the earth for forty days and forty nights…” Then verse 10 says, “And after seven days the floodwaters came upon the earth.” Same number, same result. God said it, and it happened just as He said.

The great deep and the heavens. Verse 11 says, “…all the fountains of the great deep burst forth, and the floodgates of the heavens were opened.” That's water from below and water from above. Then the waters keep rising until they cover the mountaintops (Genesis 7:19–20).
